text:
maria-support: FYI customer ACME reported a sudden p99 jump on /v1/generate around 12:05 UTC. They see 99th ~= 2.2s vs normal ~350ms. No obvious errors, just slow. They attached a timeline and a few request IDs.

sre-ana: thanks — do we have traces or spans for those request IDs? Also was there any rollout around 12:00?

maria-support: attaching logs from the customer (they're external), sample req ids: trace-7b2c, trace-7b3a, trace-7b9f. No deploy in hosted infra at that time per deploy-bot.

raj-telemetry: looking at metrics — our grafana p99 panel for "api_request_duration_seconds" jumps at 12:05 for region us-east-1. But interestingly the panel query uses `quantile_over_time(0.99, api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])` which is wrong for aggregated histograms.

sre-ana: ah that could explain it. Which histogram type are we exporting from the runtime? hdr vs prometheus summary?

raj-telemetry: runtime exports a Prometheus histogram (per-instance buckets). We aggregate with `sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)`. The correct approach is `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(...)) by (le))`. Using `quantile_over_time` over bucket series gives nonsense — it treats bucket time series as raw values.

maria-support: so grafana panel is wrong, but the customer is seeing actual slow responses — could it be instrumentation mismatch (client vs backend)?

dmitri-ml: one more twist: our KV cache layer runs as an edge process and short-circuits responses for cache hits — those responses skip the backend timing metric and only record the edge latency in `edge_request_duration_seconds`. If the dashboard mixes edge and backend metrics or mis-aggregates labels, p99 can flip when cache hit ratio changes.

sre-ana: good call. raj, can you show both metrics side-by-side? `sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)` vs `sum(rate(edge_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)` and then compute histogram_quantile on both.

raj-telemetry: running quick queries now. Here's the correct promql snippets to use (paste into grafana):

```
// backend p99 (per service instance aggregated correctly)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))

// edge p99 (cache hits + edge overhead)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(edge_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

raj-telemetry: results: backend p99 at 480ms, edge p99 at 2.1s. Edge throughput spiked ~12:03 and cache_hit label dropped from 0.84 -> 0.35 temporarily. That matches the customer experience.

maria-support: so the customer saw 2.2s because their client is hitting edge latencies primarily. But their request path historically went to cache hits. Any idea why cache hit ratio changed?

taylor-platform: looking at cache evictions — there was a scheduled memcache maintenance in us-east at 11:58 that increased eviction churn. We did not expect a big customer-visible effect but looks like cold cache churned. Ops notes show increased memcache miss rate at 11:59–12:06.

sre-ana: that ties together. So root cause chain: memcache maintenance -> cache misses -> more requests to runtime -> runtime's backend stayed healthy (~480ms p99) but edge path (serialization, network, model warmup) bumped p99 to ~2s -> dashboard panel used wrong promql at first which made initial triage confusing.

maria-support: customer-facing summary prepared, want to offer them credit? they asked for SLA review.

sre-ana: we should be careful: show them corrected charts (backend vs edge) and explain. Suggest temporary mitigations and long-term fixes.

dmitri-ml: immediate mitigations: 1) roll back the memcache maintenance config that increased eviction intensity (we already reverted), 2) add short-lived autoscale bump for edge workers to handle increased backend traffic (taylor will do), 3) update dashboard to use histogram_quantile queries and separate edge/backend panels.

taylor-platform: scaling edge pool now + increased buffer to handle model cold starts. ETA ~8m.

raj-telemetry: I'll update the grafana panel and annotate the spike with "memcache maintenance" and add a note about correct query. Also adding a dashboard test to detect `quantile_over_time` misuse (lint rule) and create an alert if cache_hit ratio drops more than 30% in 5m.

sre-ana: postmortem owners: eng-infra (memcache config) + eng-runtime (instrument edge to emit a `cache_hit` label consistently) + telemetry (dash/query fix). I'll file a follow-up.

maria-support: customer replied, thanks for quick root cause and graphs, they'd like a short postmortem and SLA credit. I'll start the billing escalation flow.

inc-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0457 — "Edge p99 spike due to memcache eviction and dashboard query mismatch". Pager duty: eng-infra, eng-runtime, eng-sre.

sre-ana: closing the slack thread — saving the corrected panels to the incident ticket and drafting the postmortem template. Reopen if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
